blurb: The call doesn't exist yet. The lead waits to be dialed, or is stopped from being dialed.
s: Lead on file
A lead record exists with a name, number and address, which may be wrong or faked.
Dial check
The pre-dial gate checks consent, do-not-call lists, calling hours and registration.
Held back
The lead may not be dialed right now: do-not-call, emergency pause, or consent withdrawn elsewhere.
Waiting for a set time
A callback or a later attempt is queued for a time the person named.
Dialing
The number is ringing, often for the 10th or 15th attempt on the same person.
No answer
Nobody picked up.
Labeled as spam
The carrier or the phone marks the call as spam or blocks it before anyone hears it.

blurb: Something answered. It isn't yet clear what, or who.
s: Silent pickup
The line opened but nobody speaks yet.
Voicemail
An answering machine or voicemail greeting picked up.
Screening assistant
The phone's own call-screening assistant answers and the owner reads along.
A bot answers
Another AI, such as a scam-baiter or a bot farm, is on the other end.
Relay or captions
A relay operator or a captioned phone sits between the agent and the person.
One-way audio
The agent is talking into a dead line and the person hears nothing.
Already talking
The person starts talking as they lift the handset.
A business answers
The number reaches a business, not a home.
Inbound call
The person called in, so the call starts from their side.

blurb: The agent says who it is and finds out who it's speaking with.
s: Disclosures playing
The fixed opening plays: company, purpose, that it's an AI, recording and how to opt out.
Identity check
The agent confirms it's speaking with the owner named on the lead.
Wrong person
Someone else answered: a child, a tenant, or a new owner of a reassigned number.
Owner not here
The right person isn't available, or says someone else handles these things.
Owner has died
An heir or executor answers for an owner who has died.
Someone speaks for the owner
An interpreter, relative or caregiver is talking on the owner's behalf.
New person joins
Another person picks up an extension or is merged in partway through.
Talking to someone in the room
The person turns away to speak to a spouse or child, not to the agent.

blurb: The middle of the call, where the agent learns about the home and makes an offer.
s: Small talk
Friendly chat before or between business.
Discovery
The agent asks what got them thinking about their bills.
Qualifying
Questions about ownership, roof age, shade and how long they'll stay.
Ownership is complicated
The home is in a trust, an HOA, a land contract, a divorce or a lease park.
Checking usage
The agent needs the person's real electricity usage and utility details.
Roof first
The roof needs replacing before solar can go on.
Not suitable
The home or situation doesn't fit a sale.
Quote
Price, system size, savings and monthly payment are on the table.
Financing choice
Cash, loan or lease options are being compared.
Answering a question
The person asks a plain question, like what an escalator is.
Objection
The person pushes back on price, timing, the roof or a move.
Bargaining
The person names conditions or asks for a discount before agreeing.
Changing the offer
The person wants a smaller system or another option, so the offer is redone.
Existing customer
The person already has panels or bought before, so this is an upsell or service matter.
Repeat that, please
The agent didn't understand and asked again.
Service problem raised
The person brings up a problem with something they already own.
Privacy question
The person asks where their number came from, or asks for their data to be deleted.
Asking about the AI
The person asks who is listening, or whether the call is recorded or used to learn.

blurb: The offer is spelled out and the person decides.
s: Read-back
Every term of the deal is read out: product, size, cost, warranties, cancellation, lien, financing.
Waiting for the answer
The agent has asked for agreement and is waiting.
Agreed
The person said yes and the agreement is recorded.
Contract sent
The e-sign link and code have gone out by text or email.
Signing during the call
The person is opening and signing the documents while still on the phone.
Credit check
The lender is running the application, which can come back frozen or denied.
Wrapping up
The agent says goodbye and the call is about to end.

blurb: These can show up at any point in the call, on top of where the conversation is.
s: Talking over each other
Both sides speak at once, or the person cuts the agent off.
Thinking pause
The person goes quiet to think, not because they've finished.
Bad line
Wind, dropouts or delay make the person hard to hear or hard to reach.
Mm-hm
The person makes listening sounds that aren't answers.
Long story
The person talks for a long time, with corrections along the way.
Other language
The person is more comfortable in another language, or mixes two.
Hard of hearing
The person needs the agent to slow down or speak up.
Speech difficulty
A stutter, stroke or other condition makes the person hard for the system to understand.
Upset
The person is crying, grieving, or shares bad news.
Angry or threatening
The person is hostile, or threatens the company or its crews.
Busy elsewhere
The person is driving, at a hospital or otherwise can't really talk.
Testing the agent
The person is probing or trying to trip the agent up on purpose.
Background audio
A TV, radio or speaker is playing near the phone.
Waiting on the agent
The agent is slow to answer and the person starts repeating themselves.

blurb: The ways a call can end.
s: Stop calling me
The person asks not to be called again.
Not interested
The person says no and the agent lets them go.
Callback booked
The person asks to be called back another time.
Handed to a human
The call goes to a human closer or supervisor.
Appointment booked
An in-home or video consultation is set up.
Gentle exit
The agent ends the call because the person seems vulnerable or confused.
Safety exit
The call ends because of a threat or a medical emergency.
Call dropped
The line drops before the call is finished.
Person hung up
The person hangs up, often within seconds of hearing it's an AI.
Goodbye
The call ends normally after the goodbye.

blurb: A yes on the phone is only the start. Success is a system that's really installed.
s: Waiting for signature
The contract is out and hasn't been signed yet.
Signed
The contract is signed and the sale is pending.
Cancellation window
The person can still cancel by law, often 3 or 5 days.
Cancelled
The person cancelled or rescinded the deal.
Financing decided
The lender approves or declines the loan after the call.
Site survey
Someone checks the house, which can change the price or the equipment.
Waiting to install
Permits, interconnection queues and scheduling are in progress.
Installed
The system is on the roof.
Turned on
The utility gives permission to operate, so the system actually runs.
Follow-up call
A later call for service, confirmation or an upsell.
Complaint or dispute
The person complains to a regulator, sues or disputes the deal.
Life changes
The home is sold, or the owner files for bankruptcy, while the loan runs.
Data request
The person asks to see or delete everything held about them.

blurb: These can't be heard directly. The words can sound the same while the truth underneath is different.
s: Really interested
The person genuinely wants to go ahead.
Polite yes, not agreeing
Yes is said out of politeness or habit, not agreement.
Polite no
"I'll think about it" or "that's a little difficult" really means no.
Confused
The person doesn't understand what they're agreeing to.
Sarcastic
The words say yes, the tone says no.
Pressured by someone
A relative, caregiver or partner in the room is steering the answers.
Can't legally agree
Dementia, a conservatorship or a court order means they can't sign.
Vulnerable but clear
Lonely, grieving or overexcited, yet speaking clearly.
Can't afford it
The payment is beyond what they can carry.
Not who they say
A fraudster or a planted lead is pretending to be the owner.
